description: Complete precision, recall, hit rate, and MRR comparison across Dense, BM25, and RRF on identical sentence-aware chunks at K=1, 3, 5, 10.

precision_1_equals_hit_1.description: At K=1 with binary relevance, per-query Precision@1 is mathematically identical to Hit@1 (either 1/1 or 0/1). Macro-averages must match exactly.

recall_monotonicity_check.description: When relevant set and rankings are fixed, Recall@K cannot decrease as K increases (monotonically non-decreasing).

precision_behavior_note.description: Precision@K naturally decreases as K increases for narrow factual benchmark queries because relevant chunks per query are small (1 to 2), so increasing denominator K dilutes precision unless multiple relevant chunks exist at lower ranks.

analysis_commentary.relevance_definition: A retrieved chunk is relevant if and only if: (1) chunk.document_id matches query.document_id, AND (2) either the chunk source character span encompasses the query evidence character span, OR the exact query evidence text is a substring of the chunk text. Total relevant chunks in corpus is the exact count of all chunks in the 3,957-chunk index satisfying this definition.
analysis_commentary.macro_averaging_convention: For every query i in [1..30], Precision@K = (relevant in top K) / K; Recall@K = (relevant in top K) / (total relevant for query i in corpus); Hit@K = 1.0 if (relevant in top K) > 0 else 0.0; MRR@K = 1.0 / first_rank if first_rank <= K else 0.0. Overall metrics are the unweighted arithmetic mean (macro-average) across all 30 queries.
analysis_commentary.k1_k3_analysis: At K=1 and K=3, RRF provides dramatic improvements over Dense retrieval: Precision@1 (+0.1000, +42.9%), Recall@1 (+0.1000, +46.1%), Precision@3 (+0.0444, +44.4%), and Recall@3 (+0.1167, +41.2%). This improvement is driven by lexical BM25 matching exact entities (e.g., ticker symbols, specific financial metrics, section headers) where dense cosine similarity suffered from semantic dilution.
analysis_commentary.k5_analysis: At K=5, RRF matches Dense retrieval exactly on Precision@5 (0.0933) and Recall@5 (0.4333) (delta = 0.0000). At this intermediate depth, both Dense and RRF retrieve a relevant chunk for 13 out of 30 queries. Crucially, however, RRF ranks those relevant chunks significantly higher within the top-5 candidate list, resulting in an MRR@5 of 0.3678 for RRF vs. 0.2894 for Dense (+0.0784 absolute delta, +27.1% relative gain).
analysis_commentary.k10_analysis: At K=10, RRF achieves superior performance over both single-modality baselines: Hit@10 reaches 0.5667 (vs. 0.5000 Dense, 0.5000 BM25), Recall@10 reaches 0.5500 (vs. 0.5000 Dense, 0.4833 BM25), and Precision@10 reaches 0.0600 (vs. 0.0533 Dense, 0.0533 BM25). Rank fusion acts as a consensus mechanism, pulling relevant chunks into the top 10 that were ranked outside the top 10 by either single retriever alone.
